_doc:
Closing something with a key or a press that is NOT activation. Framework-neutral cases: a backend passes this file or it has not implemented the primitive. `apg` records how the specification treats each case — `unmarked` is stated plainly, `optional` is offered as a choice, `conditional` is guarded by an If clause, and `not-addressed` is OURS and says so.

TWO WARNINGS ABOUT THE SOURCES, because this primitive rests on weaker ground than the other two.

First: the APG's TOOLTIP pattern is explicitly a work in progress without task force consensus, and the Tooltip contract's own status note records that. It states that Escape dismisses a tooltip and does not state what SHOWS one. So Escape-dismisses is citable, but from a page that says of itself it is not settled.

Second: the APG says NOTHING about pressing a backdrop. Every press case below is `not-addressed` — our decision, recorded as ours.
_scope:
Dismissal only: what CLOSES a thing. What OPENS it is a different primitive and is not built. That is why Tooltip appears here for Escape and not for pointer-leave or blur — those are the mirror of its opening triggers, and generating a close for something that never opens would be machinery with no purpose.

Also out of scope: a press that lands outside the component's own subtree entirely. Every component in this corpus renders its own wrapper, so `outside-press` here means a press on the REGION ITSELF rather than on any descendant. A portalled popup would need a document-level listener and a different case set; nothing in this corpus is portalled.
_shape:
`expect.dismissed` says whether the state was closed. `expect.handled` says whether the event was consumed, and `handled: false` is how a case asserts the primitive must LEAVE AN EVENT ALONE — the same negative assertion `linear-navigation.json` uses to keep a horizontal tab list from swallowing ArrowDown.

SOME CASES ASSERT THE MAPPING RATHER THAN THE DECISION, and they carry `"needsARenderedDOM": true`. Whether a point is inside an element's box is not answerable from plain values, so a backend defers those to a browser and says which. That distinction was learned expensively: the case below about padding describes a bug that SHIPPED while every executable case passed, because the pure core is correct and the hook's mapping from a real event to the word `region` was not.

cases._note: Stated by the APG's tooltip pattern, which is the one dismissal behaviour it does specify. Cited without a `quote` because the pattern page describes itself as a work in progress and its wording is subject to change; the behaviour is not in doubt, the exact sentence is.

OURS. Nothing to dismiss, so nothing is consumed either — a closed component must not swallow Escape from whatever else on the page might want it. This is the case that stops a dismissible component becoming a keyboard black hole while invisible.

OURS, and the same rule both other primitives follow: consuming a key the pattern does not define breaks whatever else would have used it. Enter in particular is activation, which belongs to `activates` and never to dismissal.
OURS. `on` is a list, and a component that asked only for outside-press must not acquire a key it never declared. The mirror of `pageStep` in range-stepping: omitting a cause is a real answer.

OURS — the APG says nothing about pressing a backdrop. The mechanism is measured rather than assumed: a native <dialog>'s backdrop is a pseudo-element and is never an event target, so a press on it reports THE DIALOG ITSELF as the target. `target: region` is therefore what a backdrop press looks like from inside the component, and the same test holds for a hand-rolled scrim wrapping a panel.

OURS, and THE case that makes `outside-press` mean anything. Pressing a button, selecting text, or clicking a label inside the panel must not close it. A backend that tests only `target === region` in one direction and forgets this one produces a dialog that closes on every click inside itself.

OURS. The test is containment, not immediate parentage: the text inside a button inside the actions row is still inside the dialog. A backend comparing against the direct children only passes the previous case and fails this one.
OURS. A right-click opens a context menu; closing the thing underneath it at the same time loses whatever the person was aiming at. Matches the guard the range primitive already applies to its drag.
OURS. The mirror of `escape-is-not-claimed-when-it-was-not-declared`, and the reason a tooltip does not vanish when someone presses the wrapper it shares with its trigger.
OURS. Consistent with the Escape equivalent: a closed component consumes nothing.

OURS. `on` is a set rather than a choice. Dialog declares both — although on the web the platform already supplies Escape for a native <dialog>, so a backend may find one cause already answered and generate only the other. That is a backend's business; the contract declares the intent either way.
OURS, and the pair to the case above: declaring two causes must not make either of them conditional on the other.

cases._bug: THIS SHIPPED. A region with padding has a band inside its own box that no child occupies, so a press there hits the element itself and reports `target === currentTarget` — identical to a backdrop press. Measured on the sandbox Dialog, which has 20px of padding: pressing 20px inside its own corner closed it. Geometry is the ONLY thing that separates the two, which is why this case cannot execute against the pure core.

cases._note: OURS, and the reason geometry alone is not the fix either. A child positioned outside its parent's box — a popover, an overflowing menu — is still a descendant and must not dismiss. The correct test is BOTH conditions: the press is on the region itself, AND the point is outside the region's box.

OURS, and the reason this is a CLICK rather than a pointerdown. A click requires press and release on the same target, so a drag that starts on the backdrop and ends inside the panel is not a dismissal — nor is the reverse, selecting text inside and releasing past the edge. Dismissing on pointerdown alone gets both wrong.
